scope: Pillars security, reliability, performance, costOptimization; operational excellence and sustainability not reviewed (by request)
evidenceBase: https://github.com/sriram-um/aws-containerized-microservices (main @ 8aae8bd: the architecture as built, before decommissioning) + read-only checks of account 977534234172 on 2026-11-01

securely-operate.title: How do you securely operate your workload?
securely-operate.notes:
Evidence: All infrastructure incl. security groups, IAM roles, encryption and endpoints is CloudFormation (template.yaml, infra/*.yaml), linted with cfn-lint before every deploy (scripts/deploy.sh). Managed services reduce scope: Fargate (no hosts to patch since Phase 7), Aurora, DynamoDB, Cognito, Secrets Manager. Root user has MFA (iam get-account-summary).
Gap: Root user has an ACTIVE ACCESS KEY (AccountAccessKeysPresent=1). Single account shared with other projects (no Organizations, no workload/account separation, no SCPs). No threat model, no written control objectives.

identities.title: How do you manage identities for people and machines?
identities.notes:
Evidence: Machines use IAM roles only (task, execution, CodeBuild, CodePipeline, CodeDeploy roles; GitHub via CodeConnections, no tokens). DB credentials: generated 32-char password in Secrets Manager, injected via task definition valueFrom, RDS/Aurora via {{resolve:}} (Phase 9); old password reset, local password file deleted; test-user passwords kept outside the repo and deleted at teardown. Human access via IAM group admins. App users: Cognito, admin-only sign-up, 12+ char complex passwords.
Gap: Human IAM user 'sriram' has AdministratorAccess, NO MFA and a long-lived access key (since 2026-10-24) - no temporary credentials (IAM Identity Center) and no central IdP for people. No secret rotation (agreed: demo, torn down).

permissions.title: How do you manage permissions for people and machines?
permissions.notes:
Evidence: Every role is scoped in template.yaml: execution roles pull only from their own ECR repo and the collector cache prefix, write only their own log group, read only the one secret; orders task role: dynamodb BatchWriteItem/PutItem/Query on its table only; pipeline roles: only their connection, CodeBuild projects and deployment group; iam:PassRole limited to the task roles with iam:PassedToService=ecs-tasks; trust policies with aws:SourceAccount. Roles were presented for approval before deploying (Phase 6).
Gap: Human access is full AdministratorAccess. No guardrails (no Organizations/SCPs), no IAM Access Analyzer (none in us-east-1/us-west-2), no periodic permission review or unused-access reduction, no emergency/break-glass process.

detect-investigate-events.title: How do you detect and investigate security events?
detect-investigate-events.notes:
Evidence: Application and sidecar logs go to CloudWatch Logs groups with 14-day retention; traces in aws/spans (Transaction Search); metrics + dashboard (Phase 5); Spot interruptions to an EventBridge-fed log group (Phase 8).
Gap: No CloudTrail trail in any Region (only the 90-day event history); GuardDuty, Security Hub and AWS Config are off; no ALB access logs, no VPC Flow Logs, no security alerting or correlation, no automated remediation.

network-protection.title: How do you protect your network resources?
network-protection.notes:
Evidence: Three subnet tiers in 2 AZs: public (ALB only), private (tasks), database; private and DB subnets have no internet route at all - AWS services only via interface endpoints and free S3/DynamoDB gateway endpoints. Security groups reference each other: ALB 80 in, 3000 out only to the app SGs; app SG 3000 only from the ALB; orders SG separate; DB 5432 only from the product app SG; endpoints 443 only from task SGs; Aurora secondary SG has no ingress; blue/green test listener closed by default (TestTrafficCidr 127.0.0.1/32).
Gap: No inspection layer: no AWS WAF (Project 3 had one), no rate limiting, no Network Firewall; no automated network protection (Firewall Manager/GuardDuty).

protect-compute.title: How do you protect your compute resources?
protect-compute.notes:
Evidence: ECR scan on push, findings triaged and the decision recorded (Phase 2: 5 HIGH in Debian base packages, no fixed versions available). Images: slim pinned base, multi-stage, prod deps only, pip removed, non-root uid 10001, ReadonlyRootFilesystem, exec-form CMD. No SSH/ECS Exec; Fargate since Phase 7 (EC2 hosts had IMDSv2 only and ECS_AWSVPC_BLOCK_IMDS).
Gap: Basic scanning only covers OS packages (no Inspector enhanced scanning for Python dependencies); HIGH CVEs accepted with no rebuild trigger when fixes land; no image signing (provenance attestations were disabled); no automated compute protection (GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring).

data-classification.title: How do you classify your data?
data-classification.notes:
Evidence: Data is demo product catalog rows (seeded) and synthetic test orders tied to Cognito test users; all of it was deleted at teardown.
Gap: No data classification scheme; protection controls are applied uniformly rather than by sensitivity; no lifecycle or automated classification (Macie).

protect-data-rest.title: How do you protect your data at rest?
protect-data-rest.notes:
Evidence: Encryption everywhere via AWS KMS-managed keys: Aurora StorageEncrypted (aws/rds in each Region, KmsKeyId alias/aws/rds for the secondary), DynamoDB SSE (aws/dynamodb), ECR AES256, S3 SSE + public access block + BucketOwnerEnforced, Secrets Manager (aws/secretsmanager), encrypted EBS on the former EC2 hosts. Access: DB only from the app SG, IAM scoped to single resources, TLS-only bucket policies.
Gap: No customer-managed keys (no key policies, rotation control or separation of duties); encryption is enforced only by the template, not by guardrails (Config rules/SCPs).

protect-data-transit.title: How do you protect your data in transit?
protect-data-transit.notes:
Evidence: App->Aurora/RDS with sslmode=require (rds.force_ssl); all AWS API calls TLS + SigV4 through VPC endpoints; S3 bucket policies deny aws:SecureTransport=false; the orders API authenticates callers with Cognito ID tokens (RS256 signature, iss/aud/token_use/exp checked, Phase 12).
Gap: The public ALB listener is HTTP :80 only: product data and the orders API's bearer tokens travel unencrypted over the internet. No ACM certificate/HTTPS listener (no domain), no HSTS, no verify-full DB certificate validation.

incident-response.title: How do you anticipate, respond to, and recover from incidents?
incident-response.notes:
Evidence: Operational playbooks exist for deployments and DR (scripts/dr_drill.py, stop-deployment with rollback, scripts/teardown.sh) but not for security incidents.
Gap: No security incident response plan, contacts, forensic preparation (no CloudTrail trail or flow logs to investigate with), pre-provisioned access, playbooks or simulations.

application-security.title: How do you incorporate and validate the security properties of applications throughout the design, development, and deployment lifecycle?
application-security.notes:
Evidence: All releases go through CodePipeline/CodeBuild/CodeDeploy (no manual app deploys); infrastructure via CloudFormation. pytest gates every build (34 tests incl. token tampering, wrong audience/issuer, expired and access tokens, owner-only reads, customerId from the token not the body); a broken release was stopped by the test gate (Phase 6). Staged files scanned for secrets before commits.
Gap: No code review by a second person (single maintainer, direct pushes to main), no SAST/dependency scanning (Dependabot/CodeGuru), no central package repository (CodeArtifact) - dependencies straight from PyPI (pinned), no penetration test, no periodic pipeline security review.

manage-service-limits.title: How do you manage service quotas and constraints?
manage-service-limits.notes:
Evidence: Fixed limits hit and designed around, all documented: target group name 32 chars (generated names), template 51,200 bytes (S3 staging stack), 3 ENIs per t4g.small = 2 awsvpc tasks (AZ placement fixes, then Fargate), BatchWriteItem 25 items (= max order lines), workload description 250 chars, cognito-idp endpoint AZ availability.
Gap: No monitoring of quotas (Service Quotas/Trusted Advisor), no automation, no check of buffers vs. maximum scaling across both Regions.

planning-network-topology.title: How do you plan your network topology?
planning-network-topology.notes:
Evidence: Public entry point: ALB across 2 AZs; interface endpoints in both AZs (except cognito-idp: not offered in use1-az1). VPC 10.50.0.0/16 with /24 subnets per tier and AZ (room for more AZs/tiers); us-west-2 VPC 10.60.0.0/16 - non-overlapping in case of peering.
Gap: Only 2 AZs; no DNS name/Route 53 failover in front of the ALB; single-AZ cognito-idp endpoint.

not_applicable_choices.rel_planning_network_topology_ha_conn_pr: No on-premises or other private networks are connected to this workload
not_applicable_choices.rel_planning_network_topology_prefer_hub: One VPC per Region and no inter-VPC connectivity: there is no topology to choose between hub-and-spoke and mesh

service-architecture.title: How do you design your workload service architecture?
service-architecture.notes:
Evidence: Two microservices by business domain: product catalog (Aurora PostgreSQL) and orders (DynamoDB), each with its own ECR repo, task definition, roles, security group, target group, scaling and pipeline. API contracts: FastAPI OpenAPI schemas and documented request/response tables in the README; status codes 200/201/400/401/404/503.
Gap: Contracts are not versioned (no /v1 prefix, no published OpenAPI document, no consumer contract tests).

prevent-interaction-failure.title: How do you design interactions in a distributed system to prevent failures?
prevent-interaction-failure.notes:
Evidence: Dependencies identified and tested: Aurora (reader endpoint), DynamoDB (gateway endpoint), Cognito JWKS via PrivateLink (probed from both AZs), ADOT sidecar (not essential: the app keeps serving if it fails), ECR/Logs/X-Ray/Secrets Manager endpoints. The two services don't call each other; separate data stores and pipelines.
Gap: POST /orders is NOT idempotent: each retry creates a new orderId (Project 4 had an idempotency pattern). No constant-work patterns.

mitigate-interaction-failure.title: How do you design interactions in a distributed system to mitigate or withstand failures?
mitigate-interaction-failure.notes:
Evidence: DB down -> fast 503 (8 ms locally) while /health stays 200, recovery without restart (Phase 1); during the Aurora switchover tasks were not replaced and recovered on their own (Phase 10). Timeouts: connect_timeout 3 s, pool wait 5 s, JWKS 5 s; keep-alive 65 s > ALB idle 60 s (fixed the ALB 502s). Tasks are stateless (state in Aurora/DynamoDB), JWKS cached.
Gap: No request throttling (no WAF/rate limits), no explicit retry/backoff configuration, no emergency levers (feature flags/load shedding).

monitor-aws-resources.title: How do you monitor workload resources?
monitor-aws-resources.notes:
Evidence: Container Insights, ALB, ECS and Aurora (ACU, connections, replication + RPO lag from us-west-2) on one dashboard with FILL() metric math; scripts/check_dashboard.py verifies every metric has data. Alarms drive automated responses: unhealthy targets/5xx -> CodeDeploy rollback, CPU target tracking -> scaling. Logs Insights on aws/spans; X-Ray traces with server + SQL spans.
Gap: No notifications to people (no SNS/email/chat on alarms); monitoring scope not reviewed on a schedule.

adapt-to-changes.title: How do you design your workload to adapt to changes in demand?
adapt-to-changes.notes:
Evidence: Target tracking on CPU 60 % (product 2-6, orders 2-4 tasks), Aurora Serverless v2 0.5-2 ACU (reached 2 ACU under write load), ECS replaces unhealthy tasks. Load tested twice: EC2 2->4->6 tasks incl. a new host (~12.5 min) and Fargate 2->4->6 in ~65 s per step, ~470-1,068 req/s (Phases 4 and 7).
Gap: No scheduled/predictive scaling; Aurora max 2 ACU is below AWS's recommendation for a busy global primary.

tracking-change-management.title: How do you implement change?
tracking-change-management.notes:
Evidence: Runbook scripts for every standard activity (deploy.sh, deploy_secondary.sh, push_image.sh, run_task.sh, dr_drill.py, teardown.sh) plus README commands. Tests gate every build; scripts/orders_e2e.py end-to-end. Immutable SHA image tags and new task sets per release (blue/green canary 10 %/5 min; rolling with circuit breaker). Pipelines + CloudFormation for all changes.
Gap: No resiliency tests inside the deployment itself (canary + alarms only); infrastructure changes are applied manually with deploy.sh, not through a pipeline.

backing-up-data.title: How do you back up data?
backing-up-data.notes:
Evidence: Product data is reproducible (idempotent seed task); Aurora automated backups (1-day retention) are encrypted with the cluster key; the global database keeps a continuously replicated copy in us-west-2.
Gap: DynamoDB orders table without PITR or AWS Backup; 1-day retention only; no restore ever tested; replication is not a backup (deletes and corruption replicate too).

fault-isolation.title: How do you use fault isolation to protect your workload?
fault-isolation.notes:
Evidence: Tasks, ALB and endpoints in 2 AZs (AZ spread verified after deployments, Phase 4); database in 2 Regions. Bulkheads: separate services, SGs, roles, target groups, scaling and pipelines per microservice. Single-location components recover automatically: ECS replaces tasks, Aurora replaces a failed writer instance.
Gap: Each Aurora cluster has a single instance (writer only, no reader in a second AZ): an instance failure means minutes of DB outage. Compute exists only in us-east-1. cognito-idp endpoint in one AZ.

withstand-component-failures.title: How do you design your workload to withstand component failures?
withstand-component-failures.notes:
Evidence: Health checks at every layer (container, ALB, collector); the ALB routes only to healthy targets; ECS replaces tasks; circuit breaker and CodeDeploy alarms roll back bad releases (rollback in 3-4 s); Spot task stop: 453/453 requests ok while the one on-demand task (FARGATE base 1) carried all traffic (Phase 8); DB switchover to us-west-2 tested.
Gap: DR switchover depends on the RDS control plane; no notifications on availability events; no availability target/SLO defined.

testing-resiliency.title: How do you test reliability?
testing-resiliency.notes:
Evidence: Every failure got a root cause and fix in the README issues tables (keep-alive 502s, AZ placement, alarm blind spot during Install, teardown drift). Load tests (Phases 4, 7). Deliberate failure injection with measured impact: DB stop, 4 broken releases, Spot interruption, Aurora switchover.
Gap: Failure injection was manual (no AWS FIS, not repeated); no incident playbooks; the DR drill ran once, not as regular game days.

planning-for-recovery.title: How do you plan for disaster recovery (DR)?
planning-for-recovery.notes:
Evidence: Strategy: Aurora Global Database (database-only warm standby, agreed scope). Tested: managed switchover there and back in 47 s / 44 s with RPO 0; RPO lag < 1 s at ~19 writes/s (scripts/dr_drill.py, Phase 10). The secondary is defined in IaC (infra/aurora-secondary.yaml), so there is no drift.
Gap: RTO/RPO were measured, not defined as targets up front. Only the database has DR: no app, ALB or endpoints in us-west-2 and no DNS failover, so a regional outage still stops the service. Recovery is a manual script, not automated; an unplanned failover (--allow-data-loss) was not exercised.

performing-architecture.title: How do you select the appropriate cloud resources and architecture patterns for your workload?
performing-architecture.notes:
Evidence: Decisions checked against AWS docs before building (CODE_DEPLOY constraints, Fargate Spot, PrivateLink for Cognito, global DB classes) and written down with trade-offs (README decision tables); the portfolio playbook as reference; cost per phase. Benchmarks: EC2 vs Fargate load tests, Lambda (Project 3) vs ECS latency. Data-driven changes: canary after measuring a 100 % blast radius, keep-alive after ALB 502 metrics, AZ settings after placement checks.
Gap: None significant for this scope.

compute-hardware.title: How do you select and use compute resources in your workload?
compute-hardware.notes:
Evidence: Fargate ARM64 chosen on measured data (2 tasks: ~470 req/s at p50 ~125 ms vs ~260 req/s on EC2); Container Insights CPU/memory per service and cluster; target tracking; configuration understood and documented (ENI limits, task-level CPU/memory, platform version, Spot). 0.25 vCPU/0.5 GB is the smallest Fargate size; CPU saturates at ~96 % under load and scaling adds tasks.
Gap: Memory use ~10-15 % of 512 MB (already the smallest size for 0.25 vCPU); the ~1.8x Fargate vs EC2 difference is measured but not explained.

not_applicable_choices.perf_compute_hardware_compute_accelerato: A JSON CRUD API has no workload for GPUs or other accelerators

data-management.title: How do you store, manage, and access data in your workload?
data-management.notes:
Evidence: Relational catalog in Aurora PostgreSQL, key-value orders in DynamoDB on-demand (key = orderId + itemId, single-partition Query). Metrics: SQL span p50 1.4 ms, Aurora ACU/connections, replication lag. Options evaluated: RDS vs Aurora, Serverless v2 vs provisioned vs I/O-Optimized (cost estimate), reader endpoint for the read-only app; connection pooling (psycopg_pool).
Gap: No caching layer (no ElastiCache/DAX - product data would cache well); no read replicas to offload reads.

networking.title: How do you select and configure networking resources in your workload?
networking.notes:
Evidence: Latency broken down: in-app 4.7 ms vs ~35-60 ms seen from the laptop (network). Gateway vs interface endpoints, PrivateLink and cross-AZ endpoint access evaluated; ALB with ip targets across 2 AZs and path routing; keep-alive and deregistration delay tuned from metrics (502s, Spot drain).
Gap: No CloudFront/edge, HTTP/1.1 only (no HTTP/2 or TLS on the ALB), Region chosen by default rather than by user location.

not_applicable_choices.perf_networking_choose_appropriate_dedic: No on-premises connectivity exists or is needed

process-culture.title: What process do you use to support more performance efficiency for your workload?
process-culture.notes:
Evidence: Dashboard, traces and load-test CSVs; every phase measured and documented with numbers; load tests in Phases 4 and 7; automated remediation through scaling and rollbacks.
Gap: No KPIs/SLOs (latency, error-rate targets), no regular metric reviews, no automated dependency or image updates.

cloud-financial-management.title: How do you implement cloud financial management?
cloud-financial-management.notes:
Evidence: One owner for cost decisions; account budgets exist ($100/$50/$90 monthly); every hourly-billed resource was priced and approved before deployment (Aurora options, endpoints, Spot); cost toggles; docs/cost-estimate.md with Price List API prices; savings quantified (Fargate -$0.09/h, Spot 35-46 %, alternatives -$36 to -$44/month).
Gap: No cost reporting/notification specific to this workload; the 'project' cost allocation tag is inactive, so actual cost per project can't be reported.

govern-usage.title: How do you govern usage?
govern-usage.notes:
Evidence: The playbook's cost hygiene policy (toggles, demo then off, teardown at the end) was applied; the project was tracked from plan to decommissioning (README progress, Phase 13).
Gap: Single shared account (no account structure per workload/environment), no numeric cost targets, no enforcing controls (SCPs, budget actions), no role separation.

monitor-usage.title: How do you monitor your cost and usage?
monitor-usage.notes:
Evidence: Attribution category defined and applied: tag project=containerized-microservices on all resources (deploy.sh --tags + resource tags); budgets configured in the account.
Gap: The tag is NOT activated as a cost allocation tag (ce list-cost-allocation-tags: Inactive) and the account also hosts other workloads; no CUR/Cost Explorer views; no KPI such as cost per 1,000 requests tracked.

decomissioning-resources.title: How do you decommission resources?
decomissioning-resources.notes:
Evidence: scripts/teardown.sh decommissions both Regions in dependency order, incl. resources created outside CloudFormation, then verifies with service describe calls (the tagging API lags). Retention: logs 14 days, S3 lifecycle 7/14 days, ECR keeps 10 images. Executed 2026-11-01: nothing billable left.
Gap: None for this scope.

select-service.title: How do you evaluate cost when you select services?
select-service.notes:
Evidence: docs/cost-estimate.md analyzes every component (fixed, scenario A 10 M requests, B 100 M requests) and alternatives (NAT vs endpoints, headless secondary, 1-AZ endpoints, Container Insights off). Cost-driven choices: Fargate ARM + Spot, Serverless v2, free gateway endpoints, Cognito Lite, on-demand DynamoDB; phase-by-phase cost history; open-source stack (no licenses).
Gap: No written organizational cost requirements.

type-size-number-resources.title: How do you meet cost targets when you select resource type, size and number?
type-size-number-resources.notes:
Evidence: Cost model in docs/cost-estimate.md; sizes from load tests (2 tasks handle ~470 req/s); shared ALB and endpoints for both services; automatic sizing by metrics (target tracking, Serverless v2 ACU).
Gap: None significant; the Aurora minimum ACU and the endpoint count are fixed costs that don't scale down.

pricing-model.title: How do you use pricing models to reduce cost?
pricing-model.notes:
Evidence: On-demand vs Fargate Spot analyzed and implemented (FARGATE base 1 + SPOT weight 3); Serverless v2 vs provisioned Aurora compared; us-east-1 and us-west-2 prices checked identical (Price List API).
Gap: No Savings Plans/reservations (short-lived demo); the actual Spot discount was not yet verified from billing data.

not_applicable_choices.cost_pricing_model_third_party: No third-party software or agreements are part of this workload

data-transfer.title: How do you plan for data transfer charges?
data-transfer.notes:
Evidence: Modeled: endpoint data processing, cross-Region replication, ALB LCU (cost estimate). Components chosen to avoid transfer cost: S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints (free), ECR pull-through cache in-Region, no NAT gateway.
Gap: Inter-Region replication volume not measured from billing data.

manage-demand-resources.title: How do you manage demand, and supply resources?
manage-demand-resources.notes:
Evidence: Demand analyzed with load tests and scenarios; resources supplied dynamically: target tracking, Serverless v2, Fargate (no idle hosts), DynamoDB on-demand.
Gap: No buffering or throttling of demand (no queue, no rate limits).

evaluate-new-services.title: How do you evaluate new services?
evaluate-new-services.notes:
Evidence: Review process: this Well-Architected review plus the portfolio playbook's lessons table applied at each project start; new features evaluated during the build (ECS AZ rebalancing, CodePipeline V2 triggers, Cognito PrivateLink).
Gap: No regular re-review of the running workload (it was decommissioned).

evaluate-cost-effort.title: How do you evaluate the cost of effort?
evaluate-cost-effort.notes:
Evidence: Operations automated: two pipelines, deploy/teardown/DR/test scripts, dashboard checker.
Gap: None for this scope.
